name: Indigenous Fire Management
description: Multi-generational human ecological intelligence encoding tens of thousands of years of landscape management knowledge. Controlled low-intensity burns create mosaic patterns that enhance biodiversity, regulate water cycles, manage game habitat, and prevent catastrophic wildfire through fuel-load reduction. Timing synchronizes with humidity, wind, and plant phenology. Oral tradition transmits observational knowledge across generations — the longest-running adaptive management system on Earth.

core_attributes.neurology: multi-generational ecological memory via oral tradition
core_attributes.pattern: mosaic burning, landscape-scale optimization, fire-as-tool intelligence

scope.definition: Biodiversity index (species richness per 100 m²) in landscapes managed with Indigenous cultural burning versus fire-suppressed reference areas, measured 3-5 years post-burn.

evidence.source: Gammage (2011) 'The Biggest Estate on Earth', Allen & Unwin; Mooney et al. (2011) 'Fossil charcoal evidence for pre-European fire regimes in Eastern Australia', Journal of Biogeography 38:1771-1783.
cross_domain_examples: Australian Aboriginal managed fire landscapes: 28-45% higher plant species richness vs fire-suppressed controls
Kootenai tribal burning in Montana: elk habitat suitability index 2.3× higher in burned vs unburned areas
Cape York Peninsula (Australia): 65% reduction in high-severity fire after cultural burning reinstatement
Karuk tribal burning in California: 40% increase in tanoak mast production per burned hectare vs unburned

scope.falsifiability: If biodiversity measurements in Indigenous-burned landscapes are statistically indistinguishable from adjacent fire-suppressed areas after 5 years, burn pattern alone is not the biodiversity driver.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Mosaic burning is not purely a landscape management technique — it is ceremony, relationship, and responsibility to Country. The 0.95 is extracted from the measurable ecological residue of practices whose full meaning cannot be reduced to biodiversity indices. Treating these practices as 'ecological techniques' erases their relational ontology.

scope.definition: Accuracy of Indigenous burning timing for promoting specific plant responses — proportion of burns conducted within 2-week optimal phenological window (species-specific seed-drop or growth trigger).

evidence.source: Cahir et al. (2018) 'Aboriginal fire management in south-eastern Australia', Environment and History 24:1-26; Kimmerer (2013) 'Braiding Sweetgrass', Milkweed Editions — phenological knowledge documentation.
cross_domain_examples: Yorta Yorta burning timed to eel migration cycle — cross-species ecological synchronization knowledge
Native American prairie burns timed to bison herd location and grass growth phenology
Swiss alpine pastoral burning: European traditional burning timed to snowmelt and grass regrowth

scope.falsifiability: If burns conducted outside traditional timing windows produce equivalent plant community responses to those in optimal windows, timing knowledge provides no phenological advantage.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: Timing accuracy reduces Indigenous ecological knowledge to schedule optimization. The relationship between Country steward and landscape is not a timing algorithm — it is accumulated multi-generational attentiveness, embedded in ceremony and story. Metrics can only observe outputs of a living relationship they do not contain.

scope.definition: Retention fidelity of fire ecology knowledge across 3 generations of oral transmission — proportion of specific landscape features, species behaviors, and burn response patterns accurately transmitted from elder to apprentice.

evidence.source: Vansina (1985) 'Oral Tradition as History', University of Wisconsin Press; Morphy (1991) 'Ancestral Connections', University of Chicago Press — knowledge transmission analysis.
cross_domain_examples: Vansina 3-generation oral fidelity baseline: 65-80% factual retention, higher for ecologically critical knowledge
Aboriginal songlines: landscape feature encoding with 0.89 geographic accuracy across 10 000+ years
Polynesian wayfinding knowledge: star path accuracy verified against modern navigation — multi-generational transmission confirmed

scope.falsifiability: If apprentices who learn fire ecology through oral tradition show no greater ecological management accuracy than those with equivalent time on-Country but without oral instruction, transmission is not adding information.
scope.measurement_limits: REDUCTIVITY NOTE: The 0.92 measures only factual content retention. Oral tradition also transmits relationship, responsibility, cosmological context, and the emotional/spiritual substrate that gives the factual knowledge its correct orientation. Measuring fidelity of transmission without measuring what grounds the transmitted knowledge systematically undercounts what is transferred.
